description: Catalog of formal theorems (Lean / TLA+ / Kani / hand-proof) that back claims in the proof manifest. Each theorem entry has a statement, dependencies, and a status. Authoritative reference for the trajectory-4 Evidence Gate.

theorems.statement: For any well-formed CapabilityTokenBody and Keypair, sign(body, kp).verify(body, kp.public_key) returns Ok.
For any well-formed ChioReceipt body and Keypair, sign(body, kp).verify(body, kp.public_key) returns Ok.
validate_attenuation(parent, child) returns Ok iff child.is_subset_of(parent) under the canonical scope normalization.
RevocationCutCompleteness over depth <= 1; trj4 T0 Phase B extends to bounded depth K >= 3 (TRJ4-015).
Once a revocation enters the gossip network, every honest peer eventually observes it.

If verify_attenuation_witness(parent_hash, child_hash, witness) returns Ok, then there exists a parent scope and a child scope such that H(canonical(parent)) = parent_hash, H(canonical(child)) = child_hash, and child.is_subset_of(parent) holds. W1.1 chain-binding extension: the verifier additionally requires `attenuation_proof.parent_scope_hash` to match the trust-root scope hash (direct issue) or the last delegation link's signed scope_hash (delegated chain), closing the inflated-parent-scope P0 soundness gap.

When two peers exchange chio.capabilities.v1 feature bitsets and proceed with the intersection, neither peer can be tricked into using a feature it did not advertise (confused-deputy resistance). W1.3 downgrade-attack defense: a v2 capability token presented to a peer whose negotiated max_capability_schema is v1 is rejected by the verifier's schema-ceiling check before any signature, time, or floor check runs.

W1.2 sibling-sum budget enforcement: when BudgetRegistry::try_admit_child returns Ok for child C under parent P, the running sum of admitted child shares plus C.share is bounded by P.share. Closes the cross-hop amplification gap where two siblings could jointly oversubscribe their parent's budget despite each individual share being inside the per-token cap.

For any chio.receipt.v2 body B, the set of fields contributing to body_hash is exactly fields(B) \\ {body_hash, signature, receipt_id}. The Lean proof regenerates from the JSON schema; any drift fails the proof. W2.1 hot-path extension: the kernel mints `ChioReceiptV2` whose `body_hash` field equals H(canonical_jcs(ReceiptV2BodyHashInput)) at production mint time, and the replay store keys on body_hash exclusively (the legacy UUIDv7 alias is non-authoritative).

trj4_proposed_theorems.statement: If child.is_subset_of(parent) holds, then compute_attenuation_witness(parent, child) returns Ok with a witness w such that verify_attenuation_witness(H(canonical(parent)), H(canonical(child)), w) returns Ok.
Under the standard SHA-256 collision-resistance assumption, distinct ReceiptV2BodyHashInput values produce distinct body_hash values with negligible collision probability.
Under the verifier rule child.dag_ordinal > max(parent.dag_ordinal) for all parents in parent_receipt_ids, the receipt DAG is acyclic across any number of independent kernel clock domains.
For any Merkle tree T over leaves L_1..L_N and any inclusion proof P_i for leaf L_i, verify_inclusion(L_i, P_i, root(T)) returns Ok iff P_i is the canonical inclusion path.

Once a chio.anchor_batch.v1 root R is published to a public witness lane with verifier-trusted lane evidence at time t, any subsequent batch B' with the same checkpoint_ids but a different root R' is detectable by any verifier that queries the witness lane. OTS satisfies this theorem only after receipts carry trusted Bitcoin header or calendar-backed commitment evidence.
A hybrid:<classical>:<pq>:<alg_set> signature verifies if and only if BOTH the classical and the PQ signatures verify under their respective public keys. Forgery requires breaking either primitive.
If QuorumPolicy.min_tier is T, any peer admitted through KernelTrustExchange has a signed conformance_tier >= T in its accepted handshake challenge.
